note: Wren Phonics Phase 4, planned by word structure (Ealing review, 2026-10-13). Phase 4 teaches no new graphemes: children read and spell words with adjacent consonants, blending each consonant sound they already know (DfE validation Note 1: /s/+/p/+/l/, not /spl/; Reading Framework 2023 p.45). The order follows the 2007 Letters and Sounds Phase 4 shape (CVCC, then CCVC, then longer words). 'unlocks' lists the adjacent-consonant spellings the decodability checker starts accepting that week; they are never taught as sounds or shown as one grapheme card.

structures.label: CVCC words
structures.title: Two consonant sounds together at the end
structures.explanation: Words that end with two consonant sounds, like tent and milk. Say every sound, then blend: t-e-n-t, tent. Do not squash the last two sounds into one.

structures.label: CCVC words
structures.title: Two consonant sounds together at the start
structures.explanation: Words that start with two consonant sounds, like stop and frog. Say every sound, then blend: s-t-o-p, stop. For a sound you can hold (s, f, l), hold it and slide into the next one.

structures.label: CCVCC words
structures.title: Two consonant sounds at the start and two at the end
structures.explanation: Both skills in one word: crisp, trust, frost. Say every sound, left to right, then blend.

structures.label: Two-syllable words
structures.title: Longer words with two syllables
structures.explanation: Clap the two beats first (sand-pit), read each chunk sound by sound, then put the chunks together.

structures.label: With sh, ch, th and ng
structures.title: Adjacent consonants in words with sh, ch, th or ng
structures.explanation: A digraph is still one sound: in chest, ch is one sound and s-t are two. Count the sounds, then blend: ch-e-s-t, four sounds.

structures.label: With long vowel sounds
structures.title: Adjacent consonants in words with long vowel sounds
structures.explanation: The vowel digraph is one sound: tr-ai-n is four sounds, t-r-ai-n. Spot the digraph first, then blend every sound.

structures.label: Three consonants together
structures.title: Three consonant sounds together
structures.explanation: Some words start with three consonant sounds: s-t-r in strap, s-p-l in split. Each is its own sound; say all three, then blend.

structures.label: Longer and compound words
structures.title: Longer words and compound words
structures.explanation: Two short words joined together (farm + yard) or a longer word in two beats. Find the chunks, read each one, then blend them together.
